PullRequest.Title: agentHost: own Copilot troubleshooting through the SDK skill provider

## Summary

Move `/troubleshoot` from the Agents Window's bundled skills into the Copilot Agent Host's SDK `skillProvider`.

- Define the skill Markdown in code and enrich it through `readSkill()` with the exact SDK conversation's host-local `events.jsonl` path and resolved Copilot session-state directory. This covers create, resume, and peer conversations without selecting whichever log was modified most recently or adding bundler resource-copy rules.
- Use standard session-reference attachments for other sessions. Unify inline references with that attachment type and remove `_augmentOptionsForTroubleshoot`, its private marker, and prompt rewriting.
- Resolve referenced Agent Host state files through their owning connection's `getSessionStateFile`, using advertised backend identities. Preserve connection URI boundaries, including references to another host; retain legacy path reconstruction only for extension-owned `copilotcli` sessions.
- Preserve the session-reference marker, display name, and metadata when editing and resending requests. Keep queued additions/edits intact while state-file lookups await, and honor cancellation during fork preparation.
- Register the extension's extension-log troubleshooting skill only for `local` sessions.
- Publish the host-owned skill through the existing read-only built-in resource store, preserve built-in provenance in customization editors, reject writes locally and through Agent Host resource projections, and preserve readable invocation links for live and restored history.
- Preserve virtual-workspace skill disabling and update accessibility help and ownership documentation.

This is independent of #346207: it does not change `agent-customization` registration.

## Review Notes

Referenced sessions take precedence over the current conversation, including follow-up questions. Current-conversation paths enter the prompt only when the skill is read, not on every request. Existing attachment, permission, and protocol contracts are reused; no new managed control or protocol field is introduced.

SDK-provided invocation names take precedence over same-named disk skills under the SDK catalog contract. The host-owned `troubleshoot` therefore reserves that invocation name.

The inlined Markdown was compared with the previous asset and is byte-for-byte identical. The previous asset-packaging rules and packaging-only test are removed.

### Validation Limits

The browser-runner attempt below failed before executing tests because sandbox policy denied its local server listen operation (`listen EPERM ::1`). An earlier Electron-backed attempt was also blocked during Electron startup. The widget edit/resend, customization item projection, state-file forwarding, queue race, and fork cancellation browser regressions are added and type-checked, but await browser CI execution.

```sh
pnpm run test-browser-no-install --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/requestParser/chatRequestParser.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentCustomizationItemProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts --browser chromium --grep 'inline session references|inline session references preserve|host-owned troubleshooting|session reference|session references|references on another host'
```

Live remote-provider flows and provider end-to-end replay suites were not run.

To exercise the behavior, invoke `/troubleshoot` in a Copilot Agent Host conversation, then attach another session with `#session` and ask about it with or without the slash command. The host skill should select the exact current log without an attachment, and the attached session's state file when one is supplied. Edit/resend should retain the reference. Extension-local troubleshooting continues to use extension debug logs.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed entry kind, its unchanged conversion into a Resource attachment, and the Resource-to-SDK-file call path are explicit. Provider captures establish eager pre-request file metadata generation, including line counts. Exact scan duration varies with disk/cache state, but the log's realistic hundreds-of-MB size is documented in this diff.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Bytes read from each attached `events.jsonl` and associated filesystem I/O/CPU for SDK attachment preprocessing.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with the total byte size of referenced session logs and repeats for each referenced session on each send or edit/resend; there is no deduplication or size gate on this path.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased send latency and avoidable filesystem I/O before the model request begins.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, the completion produced a private generic marker. `SessionsManagementService._augmentOptionsForTroubleshoot` removed that marker from outgoing attachments and, only for `/troubleshoot`, appended the log path as prompt text; ordinary requests sent no event-log attachment and troubleshoot requests did not pass the log through SDK file-attachment preprocessing.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new session-reference branch turns every accepted `#session` token into a `sessionReference` entry. The existing Agent Host conversion then emits both a simple attachment and a `MessageAttachmentKind.Resource` for that session's `events.jsonl`, which Copilot converts to an SDK `file` attachment before calling `session.send`.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 241 changes the parsed variable from the former generic private marker into `kind: 'sessionReference'`; that is the discriminator that activates the existing trajectory Resource-attachment branch. The same PR deletes the old send-time code that stripped the marker and appended only a path string.
Findings.Title: Keep session event logs out of eager file attachments
Findings.Impact: Attaching a long-running session can make request dispatch perform a full-file pass just to prepare the SDK file attachment, delaying the first model request and generating substantial disk I/O; editing/resending or attaching multiple sessions repeats that cost.
Findings.Evidence: The added return at line 241 reaches `AgentHostSessionHandler._convertVariableToAttachment`, whose `sessionReference` branch calls `_toSessionReferenceAttachments`; that creates a Resource attachment for the trajectory. `CopilotAgentSession._toSdkAttachment` maps Resource attachments to `{ type: 'file', path }`, and `_send` awaits `session.send` with them. Repository E2E captures for resource attachments show the SDK expands each file into `<tagged_files>` with an exact line count before the provider request and then exposes it to the model's file-reading tool. The newly added troubleshoot content itself documents that `events.jsonl` can be hundreds of MB and must never be loaded whole.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the session-reference metadata and host-local path, but do not emit the raw event log as a generic SDK file attachment. Send a lightweight simple attachment/path and let `/troubleshoot` or the agent's tools stream and narrow the log on demand; if generic session context requires eager content, enforce a byte/line cap before creating the attachment.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or resume a non-virtual Copilot Agent Host conversation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session configuration now constructs a fixed SDK skill provider before SDK session creation; construction only joins two URIs and captures them. The 17 KB skill body is not copied until `readSkill`, so it is off the normal startup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing SDK session creation and provider startup
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One startup operation per created or resumed conversation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The SDK session was created without this provider and discovered the packaged disk skill instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing boundary remains on session startup; the changed provider construction adds only bounded in-process metadata before it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously created/resumed conversations; each gets one small provider closure.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One provider instance per SDK conversation; concurrent conversations do not share mutable state or trigger changed filesystem work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is needed for fixed descriptors. Skill Markdown remains module-level and is copied only on invocation; cold and warm startup perform the same bounded work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed construction and launch placement are explicit and contain no I/O.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK-internal catalog handling is not visible, but snapshots show one skill replaces the prior disk entry rather than adding an unbounded catalog.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The SDK resolves the command, calls `readSkill`, performs one abort check and one fixed-size string replacement, then proceeds through the existing model request. No log is read by the provider itself; later log inspection is agent-directed and user-requested.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing model request after slash-command resolution
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider request plus any user-requested troubleshooting tool calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The packaged disk skill was loaded and then used shell/file tools to discover and inspect a log.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The fixed-size skill read precedes the request but adds no boundary; subsequent model/tool boundaries are inherent to troubleshooting.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Agent-directed streaming or narrowed reads of the selected events log
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One streaming triage pass followed by targeted reads as needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior skill also instructed the agent to inspect the events log, though it discovered the newest file rather than receiving the exact path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after the model chooses troubleshooting tools, not during provider skill registration/read.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Size of the current `events.jsonl`; the skill explicitly requires constant-memory streaming and targeted slices.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One command invocation per turn; tool calls are model-directed and not newly burst by provider registration.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No content cache; exact paths are captured per conversation, avoiding stale cross-session cache keys. OS filesystem caching may affect later tool reads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: `readSkill` has no asynchronous or filesystem calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Tool choices vary by model, but provider-side work is bounded and the expensive log reads are intentional.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression for current-conversation troubleshooting.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send or edit/resend a request containing one or more `#session` references
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The added parser branch creates `sessionReference` entries. The Agent Host handler synchronously turns each into a simple attachment plus an `events.jsonl` Resource attachment; Copilot maps each Resource to an SDK file attachment, and SDK attachment processing completes before the provider request can be sent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: SDK preprocessing of each attached `events.jsonl`, including determining the exact line count shown in `<tagged_files>`
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One raw log attachment per accepted session reference per send; no changed-path deduplication, size gate, or coalescing is present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The private marker was stripped. `/troubleshoot` received only a path string, and other requests received no event-log attachment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the model provider request is formed; cost grows with total attached log bytes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing SDK/model provider request carrying the tagged file references
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider request per send after all attachments are prepared.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request boundary existed without raw event logs in its attachment batch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing request is delayed by the newly activated file-attachment preprocessing.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective number of accepted session references, commonly one but potentially several, multiplied by each referenced log's byte size; this diff documents logs can reach hundreds of MB.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Workbench attachment conversion is synchronous; Copilot maps attachment objects with `Promise.all`, but the SDK receives the complete batch in one `session.send` and prepares tagged-file metadata before the provider call. Parallel mapping does not bound aggregate bytes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no application cache or negative cache on attachment preparation. Warm OS cache can reduce physical I/O but does not remove repeated byte scanning on resend.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the discriminator, Resource conversion, SDK file mapping, and provider captures are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact SDK scan throughput and OS-cache hit rate vary, but the changed Resource-to-file path and pre-request line-count generation are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity eager filesystem work; finding submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open `#session:` completions and accept a session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The completion providers enumerate and sort available sessions, then insert a dynamic variable. The changed lines only standardize the variable ID, title, and URI payload.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing asynchronous session catalog enumeration for workbench chat completions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider enumeration while the `#session:` suggest list is active, with one result per catalog session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same catalog providers were enumerated and sorted; only the accepted reference shape differed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can affect suggestion latency, but its enumeration/sort frequency and cardinality are unchanged by this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of catalog sessions after provider filtering; Agents Window completion similarly maps its already-held session list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider groups are consumed through the existing async iterator; no new parallel requests are introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Catalog caching is owned by existing session services; this diff neither invalidates nor bypasses it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed hunks are limited to attachment fields after enumeration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific catalog costs vary, but no changed line increases them.

Scenarios.Scenario: Publish host-owned skill customization metadata and render restored skill/session references
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Customization refresh adds one fixed directory/child object; edit/resend restores a bounded reference object; tool display suppresses a file URI for SDK skills. All changed work is synchronous object construction on existing refresh/render paths.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of customization refreshes, restored references, or rendered skill invocations; each changed operation is constant work per existing item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No changed asynchronous work or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new retained map or cache. Built-in content remains module-scoped and customization objects are recreated with the existing publication result.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed code contains no transitive I/O on these paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Refresh frequency is subsystem-dependent, but per-refresh added allocation is two small objects.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable rendering, memory, or publication regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 47 changed files and paginated diffs. The only high-confidence regression is the newly activated raw event-log file attachment on `#session` sends, which places log-size-dependent filesystem work before request dispatch. Startup skill registration, lazy skill reads, completions, customization publication, edit restoration, and display changes remain bounded or preserve existing boundary cardinality.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
